::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Nov 1st [1865]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library Add MSS 54920: 117-8
:::

Dear [Mr Macmillan](people/person_939.qmd)
By no means did I mean the graceful little lamp on [Golden Deeds](cmy_books/cmybook_51.qmd) - nor the Dove in the [Sunday Book](other_books/otherbook_377.qmd) - nor the well in [Cawnpore](other_books/otherbook_406.qmd). I meant such a high priest and book as are outside Smith’s [Biblical dictionary](other_books/otherbook_389.qmd); or some of the whole pictures of men and women one often sees upon books, - spoiling the whole effect of the real [illustration](organizations/other_167.qmd) within. It was odd that I asked my [mother](people/person_1606.qmd) if she thought what I said could be supposed to apply to Golden Deeds and she said - no by no means.[^1]

The Montfort arms are a lion. I will get the description soon but it need not be a formal shield like the arms on a peerage, but a sort of trophy, perhaps a helmet, shield and broken sword /& spear\\, which would answer to the memory of old Montfort that pervades the [whole](cmy_books/cmybook_61.qmd). If the design formed a vignette on the title page it might have the motto -

But he the chieftain of them all
His sword hangs rusting on the wall
Beside his broken spear.[^2]

I send the bit of preface, and shall be glad to have the proofs - the long concluding chapter wants to be divided and furnished with mottoes. The <u>to be continued</u> was a mistake that I ought to have corrected.

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: They were discussing plans for illustrating *The Prince and the Page*.
[^2]: Walter Scott, *The Lay of the Last Minstrel* I, 7.
